clue.text: Ban professional stylish writer

parts.note: a professional is a pro for short
a scribe is a writer, here one who wields a stylus, hence 'stylish'

explanation.surface: An expert penman of great flair is barred from working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stylish' looks like praise but punningly means one using a stylus, a scribe.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe something is to forbid or outlaw it.

clue.text: Decide to do all the clues again

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning once more
working out every clue is to solve the puzzle

explanation.surface: A frustrated solver decides to start the whole puzzle over.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve is to make up one's mind, a synonym of deciding.

clue.text: Five and four go in certain to come out alive again

indicators.note: the Roman numerals are told to enter the word meaning certain, so it is a container

parts.note: certain means sure
V is the Roman numeral for five
IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: A grim tally of nine men entering danger, sure to emerge alive once more.
explanation.walkthrough: V and IV (five and four in Roman numerals) go inside SURE; 'again' is left as a loose link.
explanation.definitionFit: To survive is to live through a danger and emerge still breathing.

clue.text: Embarrassed, but was not frightened by Communist threat

parts.note: Red is the usual crossword term for a Communist, here the 'Red menace'
to face something is to confront it bravely

explanation.surface: Someone stood up to the Communist menace yet ended up blushing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets one who faced the Red threat; read the pieces as RED then FACED.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-faced describes someone flushed with shame, embarrassed.

clue.text: Attempt by leaderless BEF to take defended base

indicators.note: without its leader, the first letter of BEF is dropped

parts.note: a fort is a fortified military base

explanation.surface: The British Expeditionary Force attacks a stronghold without its commander.
explanation.walkthrough: BEF is the British Expeditionary Force of the World Wars; minus its B it gives EF.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort is a try or an endeavour.

clue.text: Weather prospects ruined forests around California

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit around the state abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: Wildfire outlook: Californian woodland destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: FORESTS opens up 'around' CA, splitting as FORE and STS; 'ruined' adds no rearrangement, as the word is only split, so it serves the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Forecasts are predictions, here the meteorologist's outlook.

clue.text: am bent after shuffling around

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'am bent after shuffling around' begins lower-case and is cut short: the anagram fodder lacks the I the answer needs and no definition is left; a search found no fuller text.

clue.text: Bury dictionary which is subject to ban

parts.note: to inter is to bury

explanation.surface: Burying a reference book that has been banned.
explanation.definitionFit: An interdict is an official prohibition, especially a church or court ban.

clue.text: Divers cold-blooded males

parts.note: a frog is an amphibian, a cold-blooded creature
men are males

explanation.surface: Divers described as reptilian-hearted men.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogmen are underwater swimmers in wetsuits and flippers, typically military.

clue.text: One of the steps feet apart

parts.note: a means one
a stride is a long step

explanation.surface: A dance instruction: one step, feet spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Astride means with legs straddled wide.

clue.text: Once adopted it would ensure synchronising European clocks

definitions.text: adopted it would ensure synchronising European clocks
definitions.meaning: a single shared time zone across Europe would make every clock agree

explanation.surface: A proposal for one time zone so all Europe's clocks agree.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time means former, and read as two words it is a single time zone.

clue.text: Everyone needs one gun otherwise it may escape the river safari

definitions.text: it may escape the river safari

parts.note: all means everyone
I is the Roman numeral one
gat is slang for a gun
or means otherwise

explanation.surface: Everyone on a river safari needs a gun, or the beast might get away.
explanation.definitionFit: A large reptile of rivers that safari-goers hope to glimpse.

clue.text: Stable diet of porridge

definitions.meaning: oats and meal are what a horse in a stable eats
porridge is made from ground oats

explanation.surface: A horse's food described as oat porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is ground oats, the stuff of horse feed and of breakfast porridge.

clue.text: Date ain't fixed, but it's got to

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of repaired, the letters being put together in a new order

explanation.surface: The date isn't settled, but it has been reached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' shuffles DATE plus AINT into ATTAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Attained means reached or arrived at.

clue.text: Stern parson sent back into the episcopal domain

indicators.note: the turned title is put inside the bishop's area

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

indicators.note: sent back tells us to read the clergyman's title backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for reverend, a parson

explanation.surface: A strict vicar is returned to the bishop's diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns REV into VER, which goes 'into' SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means stern, strict or harsh.

clue.text: Perhaps it doesn't take long to bake

definitions.text: Perhaps it doesn't take long to bake

parts.words: Perhaps it doesn't take long to bake
parts.note: read as a pastry that is brief, not quick to cook

explanation.surface: A quick-baking treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumbly sweet biscuit-like cake, short meaning crumbly with fat.

clue.text: Programmes of course for establishing ethnic identity

definitions.meaning: the lists of runners sold at a racecourse

explanation.surface: Racecourse programmes as ID papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Racecards list horses and riders at a race meeting; read literally they would be ID documents for race.

clue.text: Eve's mate is a worker that's hard

parts.note: Adam was Eve's partner in Genesis
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: Eve's husband is a hard-working labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant originally meant an unbreakable substance, hence hard and unyielding.

clue.text: Marine disturbed a lunatic

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters of 'a lunatic' are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A soldier at sea driven mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical relates to ships and the sea, as marine does.

clue.text: The least efficient news chief provides suitable yarn

parts.note: worst means poorest at the job
ed is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: The most hopeless editor supplies a fitting tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Worsted is a smooth wool thread used for cloth.

clue.text: Capet's wild appearance

indicators.note: wild hints that the letters of Capet's run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: How a French king looked when he went wild.
explanation.walkthrough: Capet was the French royal dynasty; 'wild' rearranges CAPETS.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is the look or appearance of something.

clue.text: Juvenile spots politician entering nuclear reactors

indicators.note: entering puts the politician inside the reactors' word

parts.note: an atomic pile is an early name for a nuclear reactor
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP goes into nuclear power stations, perhaps to inspect them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimples are spots typical of teenage skin.

clue.text: Warship liable to be quarantined

definitions.meaning: someone who passes on an infection must be isolated

explanation.surface: A warship that may need isolating.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrier is a flat-topped naval vessel, and also a person who spreads disease.

clue.text: A horde is rampaging about old Zimbabwe

indicators.note: rampaging suggests letters charging about out of order

explanation.surface: A marauding mob runs wild across the former country.
explanation.definitionFit: The country now called Zimbabwe was formerly known by this colonial name.

clue.text: Do I die digesting poisonous salt?

indicators.note: digesting implies breaking down and reworking, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone fears that swallowing a toxic compound will kill them.
explanation.definitionFit: An iodide is a salt of iodine, some of them toxic.

clue.text: Hour glasses for those with long memories

explanation.surface: Hourglasses for veterans who recall the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-timers are veterans, and read literally antique timing devices.

clue.text: Fee a doctor returns when one a day has kept him away

definitions.text: one a day has kept him away

parts.note: cost means a fee

indicators.note: returns asks for the doctor's abbreviation to be turned round

explanation.surface: A doctor's fee comes back to haunt one who eats an apple daily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns DR to RD. The definition plays on 'an apple a day keeps the doctor away'.
explanation.definitionFit: A costard is an old English apple variety, the fruit of the proverb.

clue.text: Current demand for public recognition

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a claim is a demand

explanation.surface: Contemporary demands for fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaim is public praise.

clue.text: Made dough, and it sounds too as though it were needed

indicators.note: it sounds marks a word heard rather than spelt

parts.note: needed means required

explanation.surface: A baker kneaded the dough because it was needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading is working dough with the hands.

clue.text: Select place at Ascot which goes with the post

definitions.meaning: the exclusive area at the racecourse reserved for members

explanation.surface: An exclusive spot at the races and something in the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is an English racecourse; its Royal Enclosure is the exclusive area.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure is a fenced-off area, and also an item sent with a letter.
